 What to know about the Iran war today:
 Central Command also announced the creation of Task Force Iron Gate , which is supposed to extend the success of the naval blockade to overland routes of trade. The group will be tasked with preventing military technology and illegal revenue streams from entering or exiting Iranian borders, including via the Caspian Sea, but it was unclear if any military force would be brought to bear. Iran's military on Sunday dismissed the new task force as "word play."
 The U.S. military's Central Command announced Friday it is offering up to $20 million and possible relocation in exchange for information about Iran's nuclear program, its facilities, equipment or personnel.
 President Trump confirmed on Friday the U.S. carried out "minor strikes" on Iran, after local state media reported missiles striking Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz
 New Updates
 26m ago
 Rubio says U.S. and Iran are not "on the verge of a breakthrough"
 Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday that the U.S. and Iran are not "on the verge of a breakthrough," citing Iran's "outrageous" demands.
 "You have a number of countries that continue to engage [Iran] with different ideas, but I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio told reporters before heading to Paris for the G7 conference. "Right now, it hasn't been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic."
 Rubio declined to comment on whether the war with Iran played a role in Republicans' defeat in the midterm election.
 "All I can tell you is that the president of the United States identified a very real threat to this country that existed for a very long period of time, and he addressed it," he said.
 By
 Kiki Intarasuwan

 56m ago
 Trump says new task force to extend naval blockade "is in full force and effect"
 President Trump said Sunday that the new U.S. military task force to extend the Iran naval blockade "is in full force and effect."
 "Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect in the Islamic Republic of Iran. Coupled with history's greatest Naval Blockade, very little gets into, or out of, Iran!" Mr. Trump said in a Truth Social post.
 Task Force Iron Gate is aimed at extending the success of the naval blockade to overland routes of trade, U.S. Central Command announced Saturday.
 The group will be tasked with preventing military technology and illegal revenue streams from entering or exiting Iranian borders, including via the Caspian Sea, but it was unclear if any military force would be brought to bear. 
 By
 Kiki Intarasuwan

 2:47 PM
 Iranian foreign minister says negotiations halted after U.S. midterm elections
 Iran's top diplomat said mediators working to broker a deal between the U.S. and Iran haven't traveled since America's midterm elections last week, citing "the shock" of the election results. 
 "For the past few days, there has been no more travel [by mediators], and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday on Iranian state television.
 "We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward," Araghchi added, in reference to the Republican Party's heavy losses.
 Calling for patience, he said it would "take some time before the atmosphere is favorable for the resumption of mediator travel."
 Various regional powers, including Qatar and Pakistan, have been trying for months without success to bring a definitive halt to the war launched by the U.S. and Israel against Iran in late February. Although outright fighting has largely subsided, Iran has continued its efforts to blockade the vital Strait of Hormuz, while the U.S. has maintained a counterblockade of Iranian ports.
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-90c7e67d 
 link copied 
 2:39 PM
 Trump says U.S. resuming attacks against Iran is "highly unlikely" if talks progress
 President Trump said Sunday that resuming attacks on Iran was "highly unlikely," telling CNN in an interview that he believed it wouldn't be necessary to order the U.S. to return to fighting if negotiations with Tehran progress.
 Washington and Tehran for weeks have been engaged in indirect, mediated negotiations to end the conflict that has drawn on since February. But talks have stalled as the two sides failed to reach agreements on key issues, like reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear capabilities. Both have put forward proposals with different sets of conditions in attempts to strike a deal.
 Mr. Trump told CNN's Jim Sciutto that resuming an all-out war against Iran "depends on whether or not [Iranian leaders] sign a very strong agreement.
 "The answer is highly unlikely it's going to be necessary," the president said. "They're a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301% inflation. Highly unlikely it will be necessary. I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don't know how hard I hit them."
 Mr. Trump will speak with 60 Minutes in his first sit-down interview since last week's midterm elections Sunday night at 7 p.m. ET/PT on CBS.
 By
 Emily Mae Czachor 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-e99cc265 
 link copied 
 1:36 PM
 UAE says it rescued 22 crew members from cargo ship fire in Sea of Oman
 The United Arab Emirates National Guard said it rescued 22 crew members from a cargo ship that caught fire in the Sea of Oman, without specifying what caused the fire or identifying the vessel. The crew members were all of Arab nationalities, the National Guard said.
 The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center, or UKMTO, a British military organization that monitors maritime security incidents, said Sunday that a tanker caught fire on Saturday about 8 nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman, prompting the evacuation of its crew. It was unclear whether it was the same ship whose crew the UAE had helped evacuate.
 On Saturday, U.S. forces disabled a St. Kitts-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, saying it had attempted to breach the U.S. naval blockade of Iran. Separately, the Iranian military said late Saturday that two tankers had struck mines in the area of the Strait of Hormuz. It did not identify the vessels' flags or destinations.
 CBS/AP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-1ef9da99 
 link copied 
 1:01 PM
 Iranian foreign minister says it's "time for the White House" to make a choice in negotiations
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that it's "time for the White House to make its own [choice]" about how to proceed as negotiations to end the war stretch on into a fifth week. 
 "American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own," Araghchi said in a social media post. 
 "Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results," the post continued. "Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell."
 Araghchi previously said that, during mediated, indirect talks with the U.S., Iran had presented a proposal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the U.S. agreed to certain conditions.
 By
 Emily Mae Czachor 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-b0e1a6a0 
 link copied 
 10:15 AM
 Houthis claim attack on Riyadh financial district damaged Aramco skyscraper
 Yemen's Houthis on Sunday claimed responsibility for an attack on the financial district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia's capital city, which witnesses said caused damage to a skyscraper belonging to oil giant Aramco. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis had said earlier Sunday that its air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles and two cruise missiles targeting Riyadh and other regions.
 In a statement, Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said the Iran-backed group carried out four military operations using ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones. Saree said the Riyadh airport was targeted in addition to the financial center, Aramco oil storage tanks, and the eastern Saudi city of Abqaiq. 
 He said the Houthis were responding to attacks in recent days on a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, and at a market in southwestern Yemen, which he said left dozens dead or wounded and blamed on Saudi Arabia.
 Aramco facilities and infrastructure have been repeatedly struck by the Houthis in recent months, with tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company headquarters all targeted by the group.
 "Aramco tower in KAFD has been targeted, that's the sure thing," one witness told AFP, referring to the King Abdullah Financial District. Two other witnesses confirmed seeing damage to the building.
 One witness in the area of the Aramco skyscraper told AFP they saw a projectile strike the building but they were unsure what type of projectile it was.
 The Saudi Energy Ministry said there were no casualties at the Aramco facility.
 AP/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-70e148c5 
 link copied 
 7:56 AM
 Israel's defense minister says Iran mission "not complete"
 Israel's defense minister hinted at a resuming attacks on Iran on Sunday, saying the "mission is not complete."
 "With regard to Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons -- alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger," Israel Katz said.
 He also warned the Iran-backed Hezbollah group in Lebanon to not join Tehran in retaliating against Israel.
 "We will not withdraw from the security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, and if the terrorist organisation Hezbollah chooses to join Iran in an attack on Israel, it will suffer extremely severe blows," Katz said.
 Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose political bloc failed to reach a majority in the country's elections, has previously suggested he wants to resume attacks on Iran. 
 However, on the eve of the midterm elections President Trump told the Financial Times newspaper he had no plans to strike Iran.
 CBS/AFP

 7:29 AM
 Saudi oil giant's building damaged by intercepted rocket, authorities say
 Witnesses in the Saudi capital of Riyadh said they heard a loud explosion Sunday morning and described damage across multiple floors of an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District Some floors appeared to be heavily damaged.
 The witnesses spoke on condition of anonymity because of security concerns.
 The Saudi-led coalition said its air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles and two cruise missiles targeting Riyadh and other regions early Sunday, accusing the Houthis of launching the weapons.
 The Saudi Energy Ministry said the attempted attack resulted in "falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building." It added that there were no casualties.
 CBS/AP

 link copied 
 5:44 AM
 Iran's military dismisses new U.S. plan aimed at curbing ground shipping
 Iran's military has dismissed the U.S.'s new task force which aims to disrupt Iranian ground shipping routes as "wordplay."
 In a statement to Iran's semi-official Fars news agency, a Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesman said Tehran had made preparations and communicates closely with neighbours.
 "The Iron Gate plan is merely a wordplay, the Americans cannot achieve their objectives of imposing ‌severe economic pressure ‌to cause economic ⁠collapse in Iran ‌through ⁠this approach," Mohebbi told the semi-official Fars news agency.
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-c55a503d 
 link copied 
 9:29 PM
 Dozens killed in Saudi strikes in Houthi-held region in Yemen, Houthis say
 Houthi authorities said Sunday that Saudi strikes killed 33 people, many of them women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, as deaths mount in the country's revived civil war.
 The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in the impoverished country.
 The death toll from the Saudi-led coalition's strikes on Al-Shariya village located east of Yemen's capital Sanaa has risen to 33, with 39 people wounded, Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi said in a post on X.
 The Houthis' Saba news agency said on Saturday that operations to recover victims from the rubble were ongoing and that "aircraft targeted paramedics with two strikes."
 "According to the near-final figures, the dead include 12 men, 8 women and 13 children, while the injured include 16 men, 10 women and 13 children," Alasbahi said.
 Saudi Arabia, fighting in Yemen in support of the internationally-recognized government, has not commented on the report. The Saudi-led coalition in a statement on Saturday said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi missile launched towards Riyadh province.
 The Iran-backed Houthis, meanwhile, said they had launched multiple missile and drone attacks against Saudi troops and infrastructure both in the Gulf kingdom and Yemen.
 Yemen slipped back into war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the conflict in the Middle East.
 Since then, Saudi Arabia has regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has expanded its attacks against the oil-rich kingdom.
 By
 AFP

 link copied 
 4:00 PM / November 7, 2026
 U.S. forces disabled commercial vessel in Gulf of Oman, CENTCOM says
 U.S. forces disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday after the ship's civilian crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to violate the naval blockade against Iran multiple times, U.S. Central Command said.
 A U.S. military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of St.Kitts-flagged M/V Huda, which disabled the ship after the crew was directed to abandon targeted spaces. The cargo vessel tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port, CENTCOM said.
 "All mariners transiting near Iranian coastal areas or surrounding waters are advised to heed blockade warnings from U.S. forces," CENTCOM said.
 Earlier Saturday, CENTCOM said "strict enforcement" of the U.S. blockade on Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz continues.
 Iran established a chokehold on the strait, a vital strategic waterway in global trade, at the beginning of the war, and has claimed attacks on tankers. The U.S. says its blockade had redirected 144 commercial vessels through the end of October.
 -CBS/AP
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-b562fb78 
 link copied 
 9:23 AM / November 7, 2026
 U.S. launches new task force to disrupt Iranian ground shipping routes
 In what the U.S. military is calling an expansion of the naval blockade, U.S. Central Command announced a new task force Saturday aimed at disrupting the illegal shipment of prohibited items like military technology or illegal revenue streams over ground transportation routes.
 "The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper said in a statement. "Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with U.S. interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military."
 The U.S. said the task force will be made up of about 20 civilian and military personnel, based in Florida, and will be tasked with the goal of "preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea."
 The announcement made no mention of how the task force would be carrying out its goal, including whether any military operations will be involved.
 China, Iran's largest trade partner, has taken to conducting commerce over land, especially by train across central Asia due to the blockade on Iranian ports. The U.S. said the blockade has prevented some $25 billion in Iranian crude oil from being sold, much of it in Asia.
 In addition to China, Iran has conducted large amounts of trade over land and via the Caspian Sea with Russia. The landlocked Caspian Sea has proven especially advantageous with a direct route between southwest Russia and northern Iran. Tehran is located just 80 miles south of the Caspian Sea. 
 Whether any U.S. ships could take to the Caspian Sea was again unclear. CBS News has reached out to the White House for more details.
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-1b9366ff 
 link copied 
 8:43 AM / November 7, 2026
 Iran's Revolutionary Guard lifts self-imposed missile-range limit
 Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it has lifted a self-proclaimed limit of 1,200 miles on the range of its ballistic missiles, suggesting the country may seek to develop missiles capable of reaching more distant targets amid fears of renewed all-out war.
 The comments by the spokesman of Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard came days after the country's supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khomeini, warned "any kind and level of threat" from the U.S. or Israel would face a response without geographic limits.
 Asked at a Tehran press conference about the limit on missile ranges, Gen. Hossein Mohebbi said, "That restriction has been lifted for us."
 He did not say whether Iran had missiles capable of exceeding the limit, saying only Iran would "demonstrate these capabilities in practice" rather than make statements.
 Iran is not known to have missiles that can go beyond the 1,200-mile limit — a range that puts parts of Greece and the Balkans, the entire Arabian Peninsula, the Levant and most of Egypt within reach. However, U.S. officials have said technology from Iran's space program can be repurposed to build intercontinental ballistic missiles.
 The Iranian military, meanwhile, said a tanker east of the Strait of Hormuz had hit a naval mine and caught fire. It did not identify the nationality or destination of the tanker, which it said had turned off its navigational beacon and was sailing in a "prohibited area."
 By
 The Associated Press 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-27c6414f 
 link copied 
 Updated 8:16 AM / November 7, 2026
 22 killed in Saudi strikes on Yemen's Sanaa province, Houthis say
 Saudi strikes killed 22 people, most of them women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, as deaths mount in the country's civil war, Houthi media said on Saturday.
 More than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in the impoverished country, according to the U.N.
 "The number of victims of the Saudi enemy warplane massacre in the Al-Shariyah area ... has risen to 22 citizens, most of them children and women, while the number of wounded has risen to 30," the Houthis' Saba news agency said.
 The Iran-backed group's Al-Masirah TV provided the same toll.
 Saba said earlier Saturday that operations to recover victims from the rubble were ongoing and that "aircraft targeted paramedics with two strikes."
 The Saudi-led coalition in a statement on Saturday said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi missile launched toward Riyadh province.
 On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province killed 30 people. The Houthis said Saudi airstrikes were to blame, while Yemen's government forces accused the Iran-backed group of having fired a ballistic missile at the site.
 AFP/CBS 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-eda9c800 
 link copied 
 6:50 AM / November 7, 2026
 Iranian army says forces learned from war with the U.S.
 Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated than it was when the United States and Israel started the war in February, Iranian state media reported on Saturday, citing an army spokesman.
 "Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said, according to the state news agency IRNA.
 "They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-f5fb457a 
 link copied 
 3:26 AM / November 7, 2026
 Trump confirms U.S. carried out more "minor strikes" on Iran
 President Trump confirmed on Friday the U.S. carried out "minor strikes" in Iran, after local state media reported missiles striking Qeshm Island on the Strait of Hormuz.
 Speaking to reporters on Friday, Mr. Trump was asked whether the U.S. carried out more strikes on the island.
 "I don't want to talk about it," the president said. "We do minor strikes. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe 5."
 On Saturday, Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm island, added that there was no official information on the damage. Iranian state television also reported two explosions on the island.
 By
 Duarte Dias 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-eb3a200d 
 link copied 
 7:57 PM / November 6, 2026
 White House offers up to $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear program
 The Trump administration is offering a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear program, the U.S. military's Central Command announced Friday.
 The reward , which is being administered through the State Department's Rewards for Justice national security program, also comes with "possible relocation" for the tipster.
 The State Department said it is calling for "information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community, or the movement of any of the above."
 Since the U.S. launched its war with Iran in February, President Trump has repeatedly reiterated that Iran cannot obtain a nuclear weapon.
 In its reward form, the State Department noted that according to the United Nations' International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran's uranium stockpile is believed to include uranium that has been enriched to 60% purity – "a level that is a short technical step from" the 90% level required to produce nuclear weapons. 
 "Iran is the only non-nuclear-weapon state to produce uranium at such a high enrichment level," the State Department said in its Rewards for Justice post. "Experts estimate this quantity, if enriched further, could be enough for several nuclear weapons."
 Iran suspended IAEA inspections following the June 2025 strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities by the U.S. and Israel.
 "The regime's lack of compliance with the IAEA on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like centrifuges," the State Department said Friday.
 By
 Faris Tanyos 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-ad90844e 
 link copied 
 5:26 PM / November 6, 2026
 U.S. coordinates with Canada to target Iranian digital asset providers
 The Treasury Department on Friday targeted several firms exchanging Iranian rials and other currencies for allegedly helping Tehran evade sanctions and fund its proxies.
 Some of the providers dealt with Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges already sanctioned by Washington.
 The latest targets were coordinated with the Canadian government as several of the individuals and entities named are based in Vancouver and Toronto.
 "Anyone, anywhere in the world, who helps Tehran evade sanctions risks being held accountable," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement .
 By
 The Associated Press 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-6deb037d 
 link copied 
 2:39 PM / November 6, 2026
 Rubio to likely face questions about Iran at G7 foreign ministers meeting
 Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to embark on his first post-midterm foreign trip to attend a Group of Seven foreign ministers meeting in France next week.
 He'll likely face questions about the Trump administration's policies, namely in Iran, after huge Republican losses in elections that gave Democrats control of Congress.
 The State Department said Friday that Rubio would travel to Paris to meet his counterparts from Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan on Monday and Tuesday.
 By
 The Associated Press 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-48dc9180 
 link copied 
 11:57 AM / November 6, 2026
 Houthis say 30 people killed or wounded in Saudi strike on market
 Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said Friday that a Saudi strike on a market in southwestern Yemen had killed or wounded 30 people.
 The Houthis' Saba news agency said the "horrific massacre" had "resulted in the martyrdom and injury of more than 30 citizens."
 The Houthis' political bureau said in a statement carried by Saba: "It is regrettable that these documented Saudi crimes have become like a forgotten file in the drawers of the United Nations and the so-called international community."
 By
 Frank Andrews 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-153161a6 
 link copied 
 10:59 AM / November 6, 2026
 Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of killing and wounding "dozens of civilians" in attack on market
 Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said Friday that the Saudi-led coalition fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognized government had targeted a market in the southwest of the country, killing and wounding "dozens of civilians."
 Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a post on X that Saudi aircraft struck the Al-Hadara market in the Taiz governorate on Friday "with three airstrikes, leaving dozens of civilians dead and wounded."
 "These brutal crimes will not go unanswered and unpunished," he added.
 The Saudi-led coalition said Friday , meanwhile, that air defense systems had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis at Najran, a major city in southwest Saudi Arabia. 
 By
 Frank Andrews 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-2268b83c 
 link copied 
 10:26 AM / November 6, 2026
 Iran's Revolutionary Guard say they have intercepted a U.S. drone in the Strait of Hormuz
 Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed Friday to have destroyed another U.S. drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
 In a statement carried by the state TV network IRIB, the IRGC said a U.S. MQ-1 drone was "intercepted and destroyed over Qeshm Island by the IRGC's new advanced air defense system."
 The IRGC claimed this was the 16th American MQ-1 drone it had intercepted during the war, and the second in two days . Iranian forces have also claimed to have shot down other U.S. drones, including more than two dozen of the more advanced, and more expensive MQ-9 Reapers .
 By
 Frank Andrews 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-320f33e7 
 link copied 
 9:42 AM / November 6, 2026
 Greek shipping firm says crew member killed in suspected missile strike on oil tanker
 A seafarer was killed in an explosion caused by a suspected missile attack on an oil tanker Thursday in the Persian Gulf, a Greek company that manages the vessel said Friday.
 The MT Velos Sapphire, a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker, which was not carrying cargo, was hit Thursday as it sailed toward Bahrain, management firm Velos Tankers said in a statement, according to Reuters.
 "The company is greatly saddened to report the death of one of its seafarers, who was found fatally injured on board after having initially been reported missing in the aftermath of the explosion," the statement said.
 Velos said, according to Reuters, that no crew members were injured and they managed to extinguish a fire on the ship caused by the blast.
 The vessel was brought to Khalifa Bin Salman Port in Bahrain, and the damage to its hull was still being assessed, Reuters said.
 By
 Tucker Reals 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-strait-hormuz-persian-gulf/#post-update-a5bd39e4 
 link copied 
 8:51 AM / November 6, 2026
 Saudi-led coalition fighting Houthis in Yemen says drone intercepted in Mecca region
 The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthis said Friday that it had intercepted a drone in the region of Mecca, Islam's holiest city, following repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Yemeni rebels.
 "Interception and destruction of a drone in the Mecca region," Turki al-Malki, the coalition's spokesman, wrote on X , without elaborating.
 Since the breakdown of a truce in July, Saudi Arabia has traded blows with the Houthis, who have retaliated with strikes on Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites that killed at least 20 people in October.
